title: Review: Biot–Savart law and Ampère's law; Force on a current-carrying conductor; Magnetic flux and Faraday's/Lenz's laws
qualification: AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MG02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG05-calc-2#t3 term and clue written for the game; MG05-calc-2#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG06-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG02-1#N.13, MG05-calc-2#N.4, MG06-1#N.6b, MG02-1#N.3a, MG05-calc-2#N.13, MG06-1#N.13, MG05-calc-2#N.10, MG06-1#N.14, MG05-calc-2#N.6, MG06-1#N.3b. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Tesla
items.clue: Unit in which the strength B of a magnetic field is measured.

items.label: Solenoid
items.clue: Long coil with uniform B = μ₀nI inside and negligible B outside.

items.label: Amperian loop
items.clue: Closed path chosen for the integral, ideally with B constant along parts of it.

items.label: Magnetic flux
items.clue: How much field passes through an area: think of the number of lines through it.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries a current vertically upwards. It is in a uniform horizontal magnetic field that points due north. In which direction is the magnetic force on the wire?
questions.explanation: The force is at right angles to both the current (up) and the field (north), so it is horizontal, east or west; the rule gives west.

questions.stem: A long, straight, solid cylindrical wire of radius 2.0 mm carries a steady current of 8.0 A spread uniformly over its cross section. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field inside the wire, 1.0 mm from its axis? Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.

A square wire loop with sides of 0.15 m lies in a horizontal plane in a uniform vertical magnetic field. The field's magnitude increases steadily from 0.20 T to 0.60 T in 0.12 s. What is the magnitude of the emf induced in the loop?

A straight wire in the plane of the page carries a current toward the right side of the page through a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force exerted on the wire?

options.text: Toward the bottom edge of the page
Into the page, along the field
Toward the top edge of the page

questions.stem: A long, thin-walled metal tube of radius R carries a steady current I along its length, spread evenly around its wall. Which describes the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance r from the tube's axis, far from its ends?

options.text: Zero for r < R; μ₀I/(2πr) for r > R, whatever the value of R.
μ₀Ir/(2πR²) for r < R; μ₀I/(2πr) for r > R.
μ₀I/(2πR) for r < R, the value at the wall; μ₀I/(2πr) for r > R.
μ₀I/(2πr) for r < R as well, since the whole current I flows in the tube.

questions.explanation: A circle inside encloses no current, so B = 0. A circle outside encloses I, so B = μ₀I/(2πr), the same as for a thin wire on the axis: R drops out.

questions.stem: A square loop with sides of 0.20 m lies in the xy-plane, with one side along the y-axis and the opposite side at x = 0.20 m. A magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the loop has magnitude B = (5.0 T/m²)x² and does not vary with y. What is the magnitude of the magnetic flux through the loop?

A long, straight wire carrying current 2I lies along the axis of a long, thin-walled conducting cylindrical shell of radius R. The shell carries current 5I, spread uniformly around it, in the opposite direction. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance r > R from the axis?

A thick aluminium plate swings as a pendulum through the gap between the poles of a strong magnet, and stops after a few swings. An identical plate with many deep slots cut into it swings for much longer. Which explains the difference?

options.text: Aluminium is attracted by magnets, and the solid plate has more metal for the magnet to grip.
Currents induced in the moving solid plate oppose its motion; the slots block their paths.
The slots let air pass through the plate, so the slotted plate meets far less air resistance.
The induced currents draw energy from the magnet, which grows weaker during each swing of the solid plate.

questions.stem: A very long, solid cylindrical conductor of radius R carries a steady current along its length. The current density is J = J₀s/R, where s is the distance from the axis and J₀ is a constant. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance r < R from the axis?

A square wire loop with sides of 0.20 m is in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.40 T. The plane of the loop makes an angle of 30° with the direction of the field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic flux through the loop?
